questions.prompt: Which config element stores cookies per thread so each virtual user keeps its own session?
options: HTTP Cookie Manager
HTTP Header Manager
HTTP Cache Manager
User Defined Variables
questions.explanation: The Cookie Manager keeps a cookie store per thread. Headers, caching and variables are handled by the other elements.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of HTTP Request Defaults?
options: Setting protocol, server and port once instead of in every sampler
Making every request faster
Adding assertions automatically
Recording requests from a browser
questions.explanation: Defaults remove repetition so switching environments means one change. They do not affect speed, add assertions or record traffic.

questions.prompt: A Header Manager placed at Thread Group level adds its headers to every HTTP sampler in that group.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Config elements apply to all samplers in their scope; a group-level Header Manager covers every sampler in the group.

questions.prompt: A group-level Header Manager sets `Accept: application/json`, and a sampler's own Header Manager sets `Accept: text/html`. What does that sampler send?
options: Accept: text/html (the more specific header manager wins for the same header name)
Both values, comma separated
Accept: application/json
No Accept header because they conflict
questions.explanation: When several Header Managers are in scope they are merged, and for a duplicate name the one closer to the sampler takes precedence. They are not concatenated or dropped.

questions.prompt: What does the HTTP Cache Manager simulate?
options: A browser cache, so repeat requests for cacheable resources can be skipped or sent conditionally
A server-side cache in front of the database
Caching of compiled Groovy scripts
A CDN in front of the site
questions.explanation: It reproduces browser caching behaviour per thread, using headers such as Cache-Control, Expires and ETag. It does not create server caches, CDNs or script caches.

questions.prompt: Which values are good candidates for User Defined Variables at Test Plan level? Select all that apply.
options: The base host name for an environment
A shared think-time value
An access token extracted at run time for each user
An API version path segment such as v2
questions.explanation: Static settings suit User Defined Variables, which are processed once at the start. Per-user run-time values such as tokens belong in extractor variables.

questions.prompt: Users log in successfully but are logged out on the next iteration. 'Same user on each iteration' is unticked on the Thread Group and the Cookie Manager is at group level. Login sits inside a Once Only Controller. Why?
options: Unticking 'Same user on each iteration' clears cookies at each new iteration, while Login runs only on the first iteration
The Cookie Manager only works in GUI mode
Cookies are shared between threads, so the last login wins
HTTP Request Defaults override cookies
questions.explanation: Clearing cookies each iteration is the documented effect of that setting, so a login that runs only once loses its session. Cookie Managers work in all modes, are per thread, and Defaults do not touch cookies.

questions.prompt: You test a site that sets a session cookie for `shop.local`, but your samplers use the IP `127.0.0.1`. Requests after login are unauthenticated. What is the cause?
options: Cookies are matched by domain; a cookie for shop.local is not sent to 127.0.0.1, so use the same host name everywhere
Cookie Manager needs Clear cookies each iteration ticked
The Cache Manager strips cookies
JMeter cannot store cookies for local hosts
questions.explanation: The Cookie Manager follows browser domain-matching rules. Mixing host names breaks the session. The other options do not explain domain mismatch; JMeter stores local cookies fine.

coding.title: Merge defaults with a sampler
coding.prompt:
HTTP Request Defaults fill only the fields a sampler leaves empty. Write `effective(defaults, sampler)` where both are dicts with keys among `protocol`, `server`, `port`, `path`. A sampler value wins unless it is missing, `None` or `''`.

Example: `effective({'protocol':'http','server':'localhost','port':8000}, {'server':'127.0.0.1','path':'/a'})` returns `{'protocol':'http','server':'127.0.0.1','port':8000,'path':'/a'}`.
coding.explanation: Start from the defaults and overlay only the non-empty sampler fields, the same rule JMeter applies, which is why a sampler's own Server Name beats the default.
hints: Skip sampler values that are `None` or empty strings.

tests.name: Defaults not mutated

coding.title: Merge Header Managers by scope
coding.prompt:
Write `merge_headers(managers)` where `managers` is a list of header lists ordered **from outermost scope to the sampler**. Each header list is `[(name, value), ...]`. Return a dict of the headers sent: names are case-insensitive, an inner manager replaces an outer header with the same name, and the returned keys use the spelling from the manager that won.

Example: `[[('Accept','application/json'), ('X-App','shop')], [('accept','text/html')]]` returns `{'accept':'text/html', 'X-App':'shop'}`.
coding.explanation: Keying by the lower-cased name makes later (closer) managers replace earlier ones regardless of case, which matches HTTP's case-insensitive header names.
hints: Process outer managers first so inner ones overwrite.
Store `(original_name, value)` so you can rebuild the output keys.
